title: One switch may not be enough
prompt:
Specification: solve(pairs) chooses exactly one number from each pair, returns the maximum achievable sum divisible by 3, and assumes that at least one such choice exists.

Does the implementation below comply with the specification?
code:
def solve(pairs):
    total = sum(max(a, b) for a, b in pairs)
    if total % 3 == 0:
        return total
    need = total % 3
    loss = min(abs(a - b) for a, b in pairs if abs(a - b) % 3 == need)
    return total - loss

evidence.title: Specification case: [(3, 1), (4, 2)]
evidence.body:
Expected: 3 (choose 1 and 2)
Actual: ValueError: min() arg is an empty sequence (no single switch has remainder 1)

recommendation.text: The implementation is NOT_COMPLIANT. A single switch is not always sufficient; two switches may be needed to reach a sum divisible by 3.
